title: Structured Chain-of-Thought Prompting for Code Generation
technique_name: SCoT prompting (Structured Chain-of-Thought)
core_idea_checked: Prompt the LLM to first write a reasoning chain using sequence, branch and loop program structures, then implement code from it.
gain_quote: correctness, 10.66% in code smell, and 15.90% in maintainability.
gain_note: Values from Table 3 (mean of two evaluators); quote gives the relative figure; RQ2 answer box states different percentages (16.17% maintainability).
effect_correctness_headline: SCoT prompting outperforms it by up to 13.79% in HumanEval, 12.31% in MBPP, and 6.63% in MBCPP (Pass@1 vs CoT)
benchmarks: HumanEval (164); MBPP test (500); MBCPP test (435); human eval on 200 programs per approach from ChatGPT
models: ChatGPT gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (closed, instruct); Codex code-davinci-002 (closed, code-specialized)
note: Targets correctness mainly; non-functional gain from human evaluation only.

title: Self-Planning Code Generation with Large Language Models
technique_name: Self-planning (two-phase plan-then-implement few-shot prompting)
core_idea_checked: The LLM first writes a concise step plan from few-shot examples, then generates code conditioned on that plan.
gain_note: Readability shown only as a violin plot; no numeric baseline/technique pair in text.
effect_correctness_headline: Self-planning 60.3 (↑ 25.4%) Pass@1 on HumanEval vs Direct 48.1 (code-davinci-002)
benchmarks: HumanEval (164), HumanEval-ET, MBPP-sanitized (427), MBPP-ET, HumanEval-X (Java, JS, Go); human evaluation on 50 HumanEval tasks
models: code-davinci-002 (175B, closed, code-specialized); text-davinci-003 (175B, closed, instruct); text-davinci-002 (175B, closed); code-cushman-001 (13B, closed); text-curie-001; text-babbage-001; text-ada-001
note: Correctness-focused; readability only a secondary human rating.

title: LLM4EFFI: Leveraging Large Language Models to Enhance Code Efficiency and Correctness
technique_name: LLM4EFFI (task formalization, logic-domain algorithm exploration, code-domain implementation optimization, synthetic-test bidirectional verification refinement)
core_idea_checked: Separate logic-domain algorithm exploration from code-domain implementation optimization, then verify candidates with synthetic tests.
gain_note: Paper's +9.27 is vs Instruct 51.14; strongest baseline here is Effi-Learner.
effect_correctness_headline: Pass@1 improved by 2.82% (DeepSeek-V3, ENAMEL)
benchmarks: EvalPerf; Mercury; ENAMEL (task counts not stated)
models: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct (open, code-specialized); Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (open, instruct); GPT-4o-mini (closed); GPT-4o (closed); DeepSeek-V3 (open, instruct)
note: Evaluated on EvalPerf, ENAMEL, Mercury; anonymous repository link.

title: Are Human Rules Necessary? Generating Reusable APIs with CoT Reasoning and In-Context Learning
technique_name: Code2API (role designation + 8-step CoT + 5-shot in-context learning)
core_idea_checked: Prompt with a role, an eight-step chain of thought and five examples to turn Stack Overflow snippets into reusable, well-named API methods.
gain_metric: Method name expressiveness, average human rating (1-4)
gain_note: Column order Human / APIzator / Code2API; human-written APIs scored 3.39. Naming judged by humans only; input is human SO snippets.
effect_correctness_headline: P-Acc 65.0%, R-Acc 66.0% vs APIzator 56.5%, 57.5%; compilation rate 95% vs APIzator 99.5%
benchmarks: APIzator evaluation set (200 SO Java snippets); Python SO set (top 100 of 5,000)
models: GPT-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct)
note: Task is turning Stack Overflow snippets into reusable API methods (Java, Python).

title: Tuning LLM-based Code Optimization via Meta-Prompting: An Industrial Perspective
technique_name: MPCO (Meta-Prompted Code Optimization)
core_idea_checked: Use a meta-prompter LLM to write project-, task- and model-aware optimization prompts.
gain_metric: Average statistical rank of %PI (lower is better)
gain_note: Rank aggregate, not a %PI pair; columns MPCO/CoT/Few-shot/Contextual. Up to 19.06% %PI per system.
benchmarks: 5 open-source repos (BitmapPlusPlus, Llama.cpp, RPCS3, Faster-Whisper, Langflow), top-10 profiled bottleneck snippets each (50 snippets), built-in benchmarks
models: GPT-4o, closed, instruct; Claude 3.7 Sonnet, closed; Gemini 2.5 Pro, closed, reasoning (GPT-4o used as meta-prompter in RQ1)
note: Industrial (TurinTech Artemis); snippets from 5 real repositories.

title: Activating Latent Security Knowledge through LLM-Guided Risk Analysis for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: BRACE (Black-box Risk Analysis and Contextual Elicitation)
core_idea_checked: Has the model analyze likely security risks of the task (black-box risk analysis) and inserts the elicited CWE-specific guidance into the generation prompt.
gain_metric: Safe Code Rate (fine-tuned classifier), CyberNative, open-weight models
gain_quote: BRACE reaches 91.2%, compared with 33.9% for Secure Prompt.
gain_note: Security judged by a custom fine-tuned classifier; on commercial models 84.3 -> 95.4.
effect_correctness_headline: Its average pass@1 is 79.9%, compared with 79.7% for the unguided baseline
benchmarks: CyberNative Code Vulnerability Security DPO (C++/Java/Python, 142 held-out tasks per language); HumanEval/HumanEval+ (164 tasks); CWEval (119 tasks); BaxBench (392 tasks)
models: Qwen3-8B open instruct; Qwen3-14B open; Qwen3.6-27B open; Gemma-3-4B open; Gemma-3-12B open; Gemma-4-31B open; Claude Haiku 4.5 closed; Claude Sonnet 5 closed; DeepSeek V4 Flash; DeepSeek V4 Pro; GPT-5.6 Luna closed; GPT-5.6 Sol closed
note: Black-box prompting; also reports HumanEval/HumanEval+ correctness.

title: ECO: Enhanced Code Optimization via Performance-Aware Prompting for Code-LLMs
technique_name: ECO (symbolic advisor bottleneck diagnosis + ROI retriever performance-aware prompting)
core_idea_checked: A symbolic advisor diagnoses performance bottlenecks with static analysis and an ROI retriever fetches matching optimization directives, combined into a performance-aware prompt.
gain_quote: on GPT-o4-mini, standard prompting yields only a 1.99× speedup, whereas ECO raises to 7.81×—nearly a four-fold gain.
gain_note: Best of 5; vs instruction-only rather than SBLLM/RAG baselines; fine-tuning beats ECO on 7B.
effect_correctness_headline: Qwen2.5-Coder:7b Best@5 ACC 74.24 vs 68.12 instruction-only; Qwen2.5-Coder:3b ACC 37.80 vs 55.22
benchmarks: PIE C++ test balanced subset (255 tasks); Codeforces C++ OOD (300 tasks from 30 problems); PIE HQ 4,085 pairs as KB
models: Qwen2.5-Coder 3B/7B/14B (open, code-specialized, Q4 quantized); GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct); GPT-o4-mini (closed, reasoning)
note: C++ (PIE, Codeforces); no own code link found.

title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs
technique_name: Universal Textual Teaching (UTT) Primer
core_idea_checked: A teacher-student-prompter loop distills observed knowledge gaps into a reusable natural-language primer given to student models, without updating parameters.
gain_quote: UTT remarkably raises the Student’s accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% and Fast1 accuracy from 9% to 35%
gain_note: Vs no primer only.
effect_correctness_headline: KernelBench accuracy from 9.4% to 48.6% (Pro→Flash)
benchmarks: KernelBench Level 1, 100 problems (also Omni-MATH-2 200 problems, MathVerse 100, non-code)
models: DeepSeek V4 Pro (closed/API, reasoning); DeepSeek V4 Flash (API, reasoning); Qwen3.6-27B (open, reasoning); Claude Opus 5 (closed, reasoning)
note: Task-agnostic distillation into a text primer; code evaluation only on KernelBench; project page says code coming soon.

title: Constitutional Spec-Driven Development: Enforcing Security by Construction in AI-Assisted Code Generation
technique_name: Constitutional Spec-Driven Development (CSDD)
core_idea_checked: Encode security principles mapped to CWEs as a versioned constitution that specifications and AI code generation must follow, with traceability to code.
baseline_name: unconstrained AI-assisted development (same developer and model)
gain_quote: Our case study shows that constitutional constraints reduce security defects by 73% compared to unconstrained AI generation
gain_note: Counts from Table 3; quote gives the 73% relative reduction. n=1 case study, single developer, vague detection procedure.
benchmarks: Single banking microservices application case study (n=1 project)
models: Claude (version unspecified, closed)
note: Single case-study system; repo is the reference implementation built with the method.

title: SecureForge: Finding and Preventing Vulnerabilities in LLM-Generated Code via Prompt Optimization
technique_name: SecureForge (benign falsification + MCMC prompt amplification + GEPA system-prompt optimization with Semgrep feedback)
core_idea_checked: Finds vulnerability-inducing prompts by falsification and MCMC amplification, then optimizes the system prompt with GEPA using Semgrep feedback.
gain_quote: We see in Figure 4 a statistically significant reduction in the weakness rates across all models of up to 48%, while test passage rates remain essentially unchanged
gain_note: "Up to" maximum across models; relative figure; figure values garbled.
effect_correctness_headline: test passage rates remain essentially unchanged (and in fact improve for some models)
benchmarks: 250 held-out synthetic CWE Top-25 scenarios (2,500 samples); 203 SWE-chat in-the-wild Python tasks
models: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B/14B Instruct (open, code-specialized); Qwen3 30B-A3B (open); CodeLlama 7B Instruct (open); Kimi K2 (open); GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4-mini, GPT-5.4-nano (closed); GPT-5.3-codex (closed); Claude Sonnet 4.6 (closed)
note: Semgrep-based evaluation on synthetic CWE scenarios plus in-the-wild tasks.

title: Search-Based LLMs for Code Optimization
technique_name: SBLLM (execution-based representative sample selection + adaptive optimization pattern retrieval + genetic operator-inspired CoT prompting, evolutionary loop)
core_idea_checked: Iteratively evolves candidate optimizations by selecting representative executed samples, retrieving optimization patterns and applying genetic-operator-style CoT prompts to combine them.
gain_metric: SP@5 speedup rate (%) on Python, GPT-4
gain_note: Columns are Instruction, ICL, RAG, COT, SBLLM; GPT-4 on 10% test sample; top-5 selection. Edits human-written slow programs (PIE).
effect_correctness_headline: baseline methods generate at least 27.18% incorrect code for Python. In contrast, SBLLM reduces this rate by 17.18% (ChatGPT top-1)
benchmarks: PIE (from CodeNet): Python test 986, C++ test 994; GPT-4 run on a 10% random sample of the test set
models: CodeLlama-34b-Instruct (open, code-specialized instruct); Gemini-pro (closed); gpt-3.5-turbo-0613 (closed instruct); gpt-4-1106-preview (closed instruct)

title: PerfCodeGen: Improving Performance of LLM Generated Code with Execution Feedback
technique_name: PerfCodeGen (correctness refinement with reflection/planning + performance refinement using most time-consuming unit test feedback)
core_idea_checked: After correctness refinement, executes candidate code on unit tests, reports the slowest test and its time, and asks the LLM to optimize accordingly.
gain_note: Printed delta (+13.14) does not match difference (13.04); vs base model, not strongest refinement baseline; tests used as both feedback and evaluation.
effect_correctness_headline: GPT-4 HumanEval Best@1 %Correct 72.39 -> 87.12(+14.73)
benchmarks: HumanEval (164); MBPP sanitized test (257); APPS test sanitized (3,249)
models: Phi-3-mini 3.8B open instruct; Llama 3 8B open instruct; Mixtral 8x7B open instruct; Command R 35B open instruct; Llama 3 70B open instruct; GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 closed; GPT-4-0613 closed

title: PromSec: Prompt Optimization for Secure Generation of Functional Source Code with Large Language Models (LLMs)
technique_name: PromSec (gGAN-guided iterative prompt optimization)
core_idea_checked: A graph GAN trained with a contrastive loss repairs vulnerable code graphs, and the repaired code is turned into an improved prompt for the LLM in an iterative loop.
gain_metric: number of CWEs per code base (Bandit/SpotBugs)
baseline_name: BL1: Pearce et al. prompt templates with security-tool context
gain_note: Security results only in figures/histograms (Fig. 6, 8); no printed baseline/technique CWE numbers; headline gains are in cost (order-of-magnitude fewer queries).
effect_correctness_headline: FT passes Overall (20 code bases): PromSec 20, BL1 11, BL2 5
benchmarks: Python code bases from Pearce et al. (MITRE, CodeQL docs, hand-crafted): 500 training graphs, 100 test code bases; Java prompts from AixBench/CoderEval: 200 train, 100 test
models: GPT-3.5 Turbo (closed, default); Bard (closed, transfer); CodeLlama-13B-Instruct (open, code-specialized, transfer)

title: Transformer-based Vulnerability Detection in Code at EditTime: Zero-shot, Few-shot, or Fine-tuning?
technique_name: DeepDevVuln filtering of LLM completions (fine-tuned CodeBERT vulnerability detector)
core_idea_checked: A fine-tuned transformer vulnerability detector flags vulnerable patterns in incomplete code at edit time; applied to filter vulnerable LLM completions.
gain_metric: Vulnerability reduction rate (share of scenarios with a CodeQL-flagged completion)
gain_quote: Vulnerability Reduction Rate 71.00% 74.00% 61.96% 89.74%
gain_note: Relative figure: 89.74% reduction for text-davinci-003 (21 of 27 = 78.00% vulnerable scenarios -> 2 of 24 = 8.0%); valid scenario count also drops after filtering. Technique value = 100 - 89.74.
benchmarks: Pearce et al. scenarios: 29 Python plus 11 new JavaScript scenarios (40 total); 25 completions per scenario
models: CodeGen (2B/6B, open, code); code-cushman-001 (closed, code); code-davinci-002 (closed, code); text-davinci-003 (closed, instruct)
note: Main contribution is an edit-time vulnerability detector; use on LLM completions is a filtering application.

title: Franc: A Lightweight Framework for High-Quality Code Generation
technique_name: FRANC repair via generated knowledge prompting with static analyzer messages (P1/P2/P3)
core_idea_checked: Builds a repair prompt from the static analyzer message (generated-knowledge prompting, three structures) and re-queries the LLM to fix quality issues.
gain_metric: % prompts with at least one smell-free suggestion after repair
baseline_name: Pre-repair top-1 suggestion with quality issues
gain_note: Only "up to 80%" of prompts repaired; no pre-repair comparison value given (repair prompts start from flawed suggestions). Mixes security and code smells.
benchmarks: 341 repair prompts per structure (1,023 total) from the above datasets
models: CodeParrot 110M/1.5B; InCoder 1.3B; CodeGen 350M/2B; PolyCoder 160M/0.4B/2.7B; GPT-3.5-Turbo
note: Repair component of FRANC; ranking component is R01309#0.

title: Multi-level Code Optimization via Mixture of Prompts
technique_name: Optimo (Mixture-of-Prompts multi-level optimization with differential profiling, mined strategies, correctness reflection)
core_idea_checked: Combines multiple optimization-level prompts guided by differential profiling, mined optimization strategies and correctness reflection to optimize code.
gain_metric: Opt% (correct and >=10% faster), LLM-generated code, Effibench
gain_note: Garbled table; strongest baseline value not identifiable (text says >= 3x all baselines); speedup 6.41 vs SBLLM 1.00. Single model.
effect_correctness_headline: Correct% 97.42% on Effibench (LLM-generated) vs best baseline 89.86% (PIE)
benchmarks: Coffe (function-level 398, file-level 294, after removing 64 duplicates); Effibench (707 of 1,000 problems); LLM-generated setting: 292/264/503 correct GPT-4o solutions
models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct)

title: Helping LLMs Improve Code Generation Using Feedback from Testing and Static Analysis
technique_name: Iterative static-analysis (Infer) feedback repair, one vulnerability at a time, with fix instructions
core_idea_checked: Feed one Infer warning at a time, with fix instructions, back to the model for repair.
gain_quote: On the other hand, the best model for safety fixes 39 out of 44 vulnerabilities (89%).
gain_note: Relative (89% fixed, 11% remain); best model; 44 vulnerabilities only; correctness not rechecked.
benchmarks: MBPP subset of 100 tasks recast to C (GEN = 89 compiling tasks x 4 models; 44 vulnerabilities in 28 files)
models: Llama 3 8B (open, instruct); Llama 3 70B (open, instruct); Gemma 7B-it (open, instruct); Mixtral 8x7B (open, instruct)
note: Figshare link holds task lists and data, not method code.

title: CodeEvolve: LLM-Driven Evolutionary Optimization with Runtime-Enriched Target Selection for Multi-Language Code Enhancement
technique_name: CodeEvolve (JFR profiling-guided target selection + evolutionary/MCTS search + refinement agent + cascaded evaluation)
core_idea_checked: Pick targets from runtime profiles and evolve optimizations with MCTS-augmented search, a refinement agent and cascaded evaluation.
gain_quote: CodeEvolve outperforms RPBD on 5 out of 7 functions with an overall average speedup of 15.22×, compared to 7.12× for RPBD.
gain_note: Different models; average dominated by one function (90.34x).
effect_correctness_headline: 19.50 ± 0.926 programs passing all tests vs 7.875 ± 4.155 (Original), Apex ablation after 20 iterations
benchmarks: Salesforce Monolith Java, 7 hotspot functions; Salesforce Apex ablation (task count not stated)
models: GPT-4.1, closed; Llama 4, open; Mistral, open; internal open-source model; Claude 4 Sonnet (RPBD baseline), closed
note: Java/Apex hotspots in an industrial monolith; no own code link (cites OpenEvolve).

title: PerfAgent: Profiler-Guided Iterative Refinement for Repository-Level Code Optimization
technique_name: PerfAgent (curated py-spy profiler summary + objective-driven loop controller + selective pytest-testmon validation + best-patch selection)
core_idea_checked: Feed a curated profiler summary into an objective-driven loop with selective test validation and best-patch selection.
gain_quote: Specifically, with GPT-5.1, PerfAgent raises the fraction of expert-matching patches by 2× on GSO (39.2% vs. 19.6%) and 2.8× on SWE-fficiencyLite (74% vs. 26%).
gain_note: Different harnesses; single run.
effect_correctness_headline: GPT-5.1 Correctness: GSO 88.2 -> 96.1; SWE-fficiency-Lite 82 -> 90
benchmarks: GSO (102 tasks); SWE-fficiency-Lite (100 tasks)
models: GPT-5.1 (closed, reasoning, high effort); Kimi-K2-0711 and Kimi-K2-0905 (open, instruct)
note: Repository-level Python optimization.

title: Static Analysis as a Feedback Loop: Enhancing LLM-Generated Code Beyond Correctness
technique_name: SelectIssue / IssueSelect iterative static-analysis-driven prompting
core_idea_checked: Iteratively selects a subset of Bandit and Pylint issues by severity and frequency and prompts the LLM to fix them, repeating for up to ten rounds.
baseline_name: Initial GPT-4o generation (no refinement), All-issues configuration
gain_note: Columns are Insecure(Initial) then Insecure(After) for Select 1,2,3,5,All; baseline is pre-refinement code only; up to ten iterations.
effect_correctness_headline: Functional correctness increased by up to 11% (e.g., 35.67% -> 46.61% for Select 3)
benchmarks: PythonSecurityEval (470 prompts; tests for 457)
models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct)
note: Input listed a spreadsheet; paper footnote gives the GitHub repo.

title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
technique_name: Self-Refine (iterative self-feedback and refinement)
core_idea_checked: The same LLM alternates between writing feedback on its own output and rewriting the output using that feedback, for several iterations.
gain_quote: percentage from 27.3% to 36.0%. Confidence intervals are provided in Appendix J. For code-based
gain_note: Baseline is the same model without refinement; multi-task NLP paper, code optimization is one of seven tasks.
benchmarks: PIE code optimization (1000 programs); CodeNet readability (300 programs, of which a 60-example subset was also rewritten by humans).
models: GPT-3.5 text-davinci-003 (closed, instruct); ChatGPT gpt-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct); GPT-4 (closed); Codex code-davinci-002 (closed, code-specialized)
note: Generic method, not code-specific; widely used baseline.

title: CodeChain: Towards Modular Code Generation Through Chain of Self-revisions with Representative Sub-modules
technique_name: CodeChain (modular CoT prompting + chain of self-revisions with clustered representative sub-modules)
core_idea_checked: Prompt modular CoT, cluster generated sub-modules, and feed representative sub-modules back for successive self-revisions that reuse them.
gain_note: Modularity result shown only as a figure distribution; no baseline/technique numbers printed.
effect_correctness_headline: 30.24% pass@1 (CodeChain+GPT3.5, APPS test) vs 22.33
benchmarks: APPS (test 5000; val 150; 20-task subset for the modularity judgement); CodeContests (val 117, test 165); LeetCodeHardGym (39 tasks)
models: GPT-3.5-turbo-16k (closed, instruct); GPT-4 (closed); WizardCoder 1B-34B (open, code-specialized)
note: Correctness-focused; modularity judged by GPT-4 on 20 tasks only.

title: From Solitary Directives to Interactive Encouragement! LLM Secure Code Generation by Natural Language Prompting
technique_name: SecCode (Encouragement Prompting + interactive iteration + CodeQL cross-check)
core_idea_checked: "Encouragement" prompts make the model repeatedly detect and fix vulnerabilities, with its own analysis and CodeQL findings fed back for patching.
gain_metric: Fix Success Rate (FSR) at iteration 10, LEval
gain_note: FSR judged with the same CodeQL plus LLM self-check (possibly circular); FSR denominator unclear.
effect_correctness_headline: pass@1 Gen. 0.77 -> Fixed 1.00 (CPP); 0.85 -> 0.99 (Python), HumanEval GPT-3.5
benchmarks: LLMSecEval (150 prompts), SecurityEval-derived NL prompts (121), Holmes-derived NL prompts (213); ground-truth code versions LEval_G/SecEval_G/Holmes_G (150/121/310); HumanEval C++/Python (164 each)
models: GPT-3.5 Turbo, closed, instruct; GPT-4, closed; GPT-4o, closed; Llama 3.1 8B Instruct, open, instruct; DeepSeek Coder V2 Lite Instruct, open, code-specialized
note: CodeQL results are fed back, so partly a tool feedback loop.

title: RefleXGen:The unexamined code is not worth using
technique_name: RefleXGen (guided self-reflection with self-accumulating security RAG knowledge base)
core_idea_checked: Have the model reflect on its code's security and store reflections in a self-growing knowledge base retrieved for later generations.
gain_quote: Base +RefleXGen Base +RefleXGen Base +RefleXGen 75.5 97.6 24.5 19.5 0.5 89.1 (↑13.6)
gain_note: Largest gain model; GPT-4o 92.3 to 99.0. Pass rate drops for some models.
benchmarks: He & Vechev (SVEN) security dataset: 9 CWE scenarios from the MITRE top 25, each with 2-3 programming environments; 25 generations per scenario, 5 repeats
models: GPT-3.5 Turbo (closed, instruct); GPT-4o (closed); CodeQwen1.5 (open, code-specialized); Gemini 1.0 Pro (closed)

title: Fortifying LLM-Based Code Generation with Graph-Based Reasoning on Secure Coding Practices
technique_name: GRASP (SCP Graph-based reasoning)
core_idea_checked: Organizes secure coding practices into a dependency graph and has the LLM traverse relevant practices to revise its seed code.
gain_note: Columns Zero-Shot, PaS, PromSec, GRASP (Table 3, GPT-4o); vs base model the GPT-4o rate rises 0.61->0.82.
effect_correctness_headline: GRASP improves the secure-pass@1 score for GPT-4o from 0.47 to 0.58. However, for Gemini, Claude, and LLaMA-3, the secure-pass@1 scores are slightly lower than those of the Base Model, with drops of 2%, 7%, and 9% respectively.
benchmarks: New benchmark of 54 natural-language prompts (37 Python, 17 C) covering 17 CWEs, 25 samples per scenario; 24 zero-day Python CVE scenarios from the CodeQL Wall of Fame
models: GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct); Claude-3-haiku (closed, instruct); Gemini-1.5-flash (closed, instruct); Llama-3-8B-Instruct (open, 8B, instruct)

title: Safety Sidecar: Reflection-Driven Runtime Control for Safer Agents
technique_name: Safety Sidecar (LLM self-check routing + retrieval-augmented multi-turn reflective repair + verifier-gated memory)
core_idea_checked: A sidecar routes outputs through LLM self-check and retrieval-augmented reflective repair, storing only verifier-approved fixes in memory.
gain_note: Middle of four models (gains +2.9 to +11.2). Denominator is compilable samples.
effect_correctness_headline: Pass Rate qwen3-coder-plus 86.7 -> 80.1 (↓6.6); gpt-3.5-turbo 88.0 -> 92.4 (↑4.4)
benchmarks: He & Vechev 2023 (SVEN) CWE scenarios, 8 CWEs, ~20 scenarios, 25 samples per scenario x5 runs; HotpotQA cross-domain
models: gpt-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct); gpt-4o (closed); qwen3-coder-plus (closed API, code-specialized); gemini-2.5-pro (closed, reasoning)
note: Same authors and method as Reflection-Driven Control (R04031#0), extended version; same 8-CWE SVEN evaluation.

title: Toward Secure Code Generation: Bridging Correctness and Security via Task-Adaptive Vulnerability Modeling and Execution-Based Benchmarking
technique_name: SecAwareCoder (task-adaptive threat modeling + constraint-guided generation + security-aware test synthesis + closed-loop refinement)
core_idea_checked: Derive a solution blueprint and task-specific threat model, generate under those constraints, then synthesize adversarial security tests to drive repair.
gain_note: Table fragment F-Pass/S-Pass pairs for Greedy, CoT, AutoSafeCoder, SecAwareCoder; column order garbled in extraction; security tests built by the authors; mixed on some backbones.
effect_correctness_headline: Pass@1 28.63 vs 23.92 (CoT), GPT-5 on full CodeSecEval
benchmarks: CodeSecEval (new; 255 Python tasks, 77 CWEs; SecEvalBase 115, SecEvalPlus 140); also an insecure-code repair setting
models: GPT-5 (closed, reasoning); Qwen-Coder-Plus (closed, code-specialized); DeepSeek-Chat (closed API, instruct); Llama 3-8B-Instruct (open, instruct); CodeLlama-7B-Instruct (open, code-specialized)
note: Paper also introduces the CodeSecEval benchmark; repo hosts SecAwareCoder.

title: SOEN-101: Code Generation by Emulating Software Process Models Using Large Language Model Agents
technique_name: FlowGen (Waterfall/TDD/Scrum multi-agent process emulation with self-refinement)
core_idea_checked: Emulate Waterfall, TDD or Scrum processes by assigning LLM agents to developer roles that communicate and self-refine code.
gain_metric: error code smell density (Pylint, per 10 LOC)
gain_quote: FlowGen decreases the error code smell density by 81.8%
gain_note: Relative reduction of a density; range 81.8%-96.0% across process variants, lower end used; warning density only 15.0%-57.9%; 3 runs, no statistical test.
effect_correctness_headline: FlowGenScrum 75.2±1.1 (+16.8%)* HumanEval vs RawGPT 64.4±3.7
benchmarks: HumanEval (164); HumanEval-ET; MBPP sanitized (427); MBPP-ET
models: GPT-3.5-turbo (1106, plus 0301/0613/0125 in RQ3), closed, instruct
note: Also known as SOEN-101 / FlowGen; Pylint smell density on HumanEval/MBPP.

title: MaintainCoder: Maintainable Code Generation Under Dynamic Requirements
technique_name: MaintainCoder (multi-agent pipeline: requirements analysis, design pattern selection, framework design + framework evaluation loop, code generation, code optimization with execution feedback)
core_idea_checked: Section 3.3: a Code Framework Module (requirements-analysis agent, design-pattern-selection agent, framework-design agent, framework-evaluation agent in a revision loop) produces an architectural blueprint, and a Code Generation Module (code-generation agent under PEP8/PEP257 plus a code-optimization agent driven by execution feedback on inserted assertions) turns it into tested Python; AutoGen is the orchestration framework.
baseline_name: DeepSeek-V3 (plain LLM, strongest non-MaintainCoder row in Table 1 on APPS-Dyn Pass@5)
gain_note: Table 1 (APPS-Dyn) is garbled by PDF extraction into column blocks; the quoted span is the Pass@5 column of the DeepSeek-V3 block, rows in order DeepSeek-V3 / +CoT / +Plan / AgentCoder / MapCoder / MaintainCoder, so 59.5 is the strongest baseline and 62.5 is MaintainCoder(DeepSeek-V3). Strongest baselines elsewhere in that column are Gemini-2.5-Flash-Preview 51.0 and Claude-3.7-Sonnet 48.5. The authors' own headline is the weaker-baseline framing 'MaintainCoder(GPT-4o-mini) attains 50.5% Pass@5 accuracy' versus GPT-4o-mini 35.5, and 'more than 60%' relative improvement on xCodeEval-Dyn (36.7 vs 22.7 for the second-best DeepSeek variant). Phase-II modifier is fixed to GPT-4o-mini; Gemini-2.5-Flash-Preview as Phase-II generator (Table 8) reproduces the ordering. Static MI is not consistently better on entry-level sets (Table 7).
effect_correctness_headline: MaintainCoder (GPT-4o-mini) achieves an 11% increase on xCodeEval (from 46% to 57%), which is over double the improvement seen on APPS (44% to 48%)
benchmarks: MaintainBench (new): HumanEval-Dyn and MBPP-Dyn (30 problems each extended to 120 new problems), APPS-Dyn (50 problems extended to 200+), CodeContests-Dyn and xCodeEval-Dyn (30 each extended to 120+); 500+ problems total; plus original APPS, CodeContests, xCodeEval
models: GPT-4o-mini, closed, instruct; DeepSeek-V3, open, instruct; o3-mini, closed, reasoning (backbones); baselines also GPT-4o, Qwen-Plus, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Preview, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, GPT-4.1-mini (MetaGPT), all closed
note: Python function-level generation on HumanEval/MBPP/APPS/CodeContests/xCodeEval derivatives, so it runs unchanged on general-purpose function-level benchmarks; the paper also contributes the MaintainBench benchmark but MaintainCoder is a standalone reusable method with public code.

title: INDICT: Code Generation with Internal Dialogues of Critiques for Both Security and Helpfulness
technique_name: INDICT (dual safety/helpfulness critics with tool-grounded preemptive and post-hoc feedback)
core_idea_checked: Two LLM critics, one for safety and one for helpfulness, hold an internal dialogue grounded by web search and code execution, giving preemptive and post-hoc feedback to the coder.
gain_metric: Safety: % outputs not flagged by CyberSecEval insecure code detector (CyberSecEval-1 validation split)
gain_quote: Direct Gen 78.2 50.0 64.1 additional instructions are given to models to proINDICT 90.9 81.4 86.1
gain_note: Strongest baseline in the same table is Reflexion+ at 86.9 safety (GPT-4o-mini); 20% validation split of CyberSecEval-1. Extraction headline CommandR 68.2->81.0 is from the helpfulness table (Table 11), not safety.
benchmarks: CyberSecEval-1 Insecure Coding Practice Autocomplete (1,916) and Instruction (1,916); CVS (500 sampled); CyberSecEval-1 Cyber Attack (1,000); CyberSecEval-2 Interpreter Abuse (500) and Prompt Injection (251); HarmBench (320 x 6 splits); CAMEL (100)
models: CommandR 35B (open, instruct/tool-tuned); Llama3-8b-instruct (open, instruct); Llama3-70b-instruct (open, instruct); CodeLlama-7b/13b/34b-instruct (open, code-specialized); Llama2 chat (open, instruct); GPT-4o-mini (closed, instruct)

title: Agentic Code Optimization via Compiler-LLM Cooperation
technique_name: ACCLAIM (compiler-LLM cooperation multi-agent system)
core_idea_checked: Multi-agent LLM system that optimizes a program at source, IR and assembly levels with compiler feedback and budget split across levels.
gain_quote: Source-only (1) IR-only (2) Assembly-only (3) Single-level portfolio (4) ACCLAIM Geo. Mean 1.18 1.04 1.03 1.02 1.25
gain_note: Both values are speedups vs clang -O3, equal budget; 100 programs.
effect_correctness_headline: Overall % Correct Generations 51.4%, % Correct Samples 69.4%
benchmarks: Project CodeNet C programs filtered to 5,640 programs (564 problems); experiments use a random 100-program sample
models: Claude 3.7 Sonnet (closed); Llama4-Maverick-17B-instruct (open); Llama3.3-70B-instruct (open); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (open, code); Qwen3-4B (open); Qwen3-30B-A3B (open MoE)
note: C programs (CodeNet) optimized at source, IR and assembly levels; needs compiler toolchain.

title: Securing AI-Generated Code: A Just-in-Time Vulnerability Detection and Remediation Pipeline
technique_name: Pipeline 1: enriched Code Validator LLM findings (MITRE ATT&CK, CWE Observed Examples, Python best practices) fed to generator for remediation
core_idea_checked: A validator LLM reviews generated code and its findings are enriched with MITRE ATT&CK, CWE examples and best practices before the generator remediates.
gain_metric: Static analyzer findings per sample (CodeQL+Bandit), pooled
gain_note: Same tools used for feedback in P2 and evaluation; functional correctness not evaluated; Claude models only.
benchmarks: LLMSecEval subset, 26 prompts, 9 CWEs
models: Claude Opus 4.8 (closed); Claude Sonnet 4.6 (closed); Claude Sonnet 5 (closed); Claude Haiku 4.5 (closed)
note: Pipeline 2 (R06501#1) is this pipeline plus initial static-analysis findings.

title: ContextEvolve: Multi-Agent Context Compression for Systems Code Optimization
technique_name: ContextEvolve (Summarizer, Navigator and Sampler agents for context compression in evolutionary code optimization)
core_idea_checked: Three agents compress evolutionary search context into semantic state, optimization direction and exemplar sampling, mimicking an RL loop in text.
gain_quote: ContextEvolve outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 33.3% while reducing token consumption by 29.0%.
gain_note: 33.3% is the best single task (LB); text reports 6.5% average.
benchmarks: ADRS benchmark, 5 tasks (TS, SQL, LB, SAK, MP)
models: Qwen3 (size not stated, open)
note: Evaluated only on ADRS systems-algorithm tasks; method is generic evolutionary code search with an evaluator.

title: Lessons Learned: A Multi-Agent Framework for Code LLMs to Learn and Improve
technique_name: LessonL (lesson solicitation-banking-selection multi-agent framework)
core_idea_checked: Agents extract lessons from each other's successes and failures, bank them, and select relevant lessons to guide later optimisation rounds.
gain_note: Strongest method baseline used; OpenAI o3 (2.21) beats LessonL; incorrect or slower code counted as speedup 1; quote is a table column fragment.
effect_correctness_headline: ParEval serial Correct 0.91 ± 0.02 vs Qwen14B 0.67 ± 0.03; HumanEval pass@1 0.915
benchmarks: ParEval adapted for optimization (60 tasks, serial and OpenMP modes); PolyBench (30 tasks); HumanEval, HumanEval+, MBPP, MBPP+ (correctness only)
models: Deepseek-coder-7b-instruct-v1.5 (open, code); Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (open, code); Qwen2.5-Coder-14B-Instruct (open, code); GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o (closed, baselines); DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B and o3 (reasoning, baselines); Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen2.5-7B, phi-4 (agent-scaling study)
note: Mainly C++/OpenMP code optimization; also HumanEval-style tasks.

title: MARCO: Multi-Agent Code Optimization with Real-Time Knowledge Integration for High-Performance Computing
technique_name: MARCO (code optimizer agent + performance evaluator agent + Tavily web search)
core_idea_checked: An optimizer agent and a performance-evaluator agent iterate on code, with live web search adding recent optimization knowledge.
gain_quote: achieving an average runtime reduction of 14.6% (mean runtime 49.1 ms vs. 57.5 ms)
gain_note: Correctness not reported; unclear which LLM backs each MARCO result.
benchmarks: LeetCode 75 (75 easy/medium problems) + 10 randomly selected LeetCode hard problems
models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (closed, instruct); GPT-4o (closed, instruct); DeepSeek Coder-V2 (open, code-specialized; baseline only); Llama 3.1 8B (open, instruct; baseline only)
note: HPC-motivated but evaluated on LeetCode; relies on live web search (Tavily), hard to make reproducible.

title: Mitigating Collaboration Degeneration in Multi-Agent Code Generation via a Controllable Competitive Collaboration Approach
technique_name: C3 (Controllable Competitive Collaboration) with Centralized Auction-Based Competition (CAB) and Decentralized Communication-Aware Competition (DCC)
core_idea_checked: Introduces auction-based centralized and communication-aware decentralized competition between agents within a collaborative software-development pipeline.
gain_note: Second row is maintainability; DCC ties NC and CAB; single model, no variance.
effect_correctness_headline: Executability DCC 86.7 (↑19.9%) vs MetaGPT 72.3
benchmarks: Extended SoftwareDev (70 tasks, built by the authors, inspired by MetaGPT); preliminary study on HumanEval
models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct)
note: Project-level software development pipeline; small HumanEval preliminary study.

title: Learning Performance-Improving Code Edits
technique_name: Dynamic retrieval-based few-shot prompting (PIE)
core_idea_checked: Retrieve the most similar slow-to-fast program edit pairs from PIE by embedding similarity and use them as dynamic few-shot examples for optimization.
baseline_name: CodeLlama 34B chain-of-thought prompting (strongest prompting baseline for that model)
gain_quote: 34B from 19.63 %O PT, 1.30× S PEEDUP to 34.25% %O PT, 2.28× S PEEDUP for BEST @8.
gain_note: CodeLlama 34B pair; Table 1/3 report 2.43x for K=4 (text figure matches K=1/2). GPT-4: 3.93x retrieval vs 1.58x CoT Best@8 (table only). Best@8 with correctness filtering.
effect_correctness_headline: GPT-4 Best@8 %Correct 95.71%
benchmarks: PIE test set (978 pairs, 41 problems, from CodeNet)
models: CodeLlama 7B/13B/34B (open, base); GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 (closed); GPT-4-0613 (closed)
note: C++ (PIE); paper main contributions are PIE dataset and fine-tuning (R00256#1); this is its retrieval prompting.

title: Large Language Model-Aware In-Context Learning for Code Generation
technique_name: LAIL (LLM-Aware In-context Learning example retrieval)
core_idea_checked: Labels candidate examples by how much they raise the LLM's own likelihood of the correct answer, trains a contrastive retriever on these labels and selects in-context examples with it.
gain_metric: Human code-quality rating (0-2, absence of bad smells)
gain_quote: Particularly, our LAIL surpasses the SOTA approach by 5.811% in code quality and 7.027% in maintainability.
gain_note: Relative improvement of a human rating (LAIL 1.839 vs 1.738); no agreement statistic; model for human evaluation unspecified.
effect_correctness_headline: LAIL outperforms it by 11.58%, 6.89%, and 5.07% on CodeGen, and acquires 4.38%, 2.85%, and 2.74% improvement on GPT-3.5 in Pass@1
benchmarks: MBJP (493 test tasks), MBPP (500 test tasks), MBCPP (435 test tasks); human evaluation on 50 sampled tasks
models: CodeGen-Multi-16B (open, code-specialized); GPT-3.5 text-davinci-003 (closed, base); ChatGPT gpt-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct)
note: Targets correctness via example selection; no code-quality target.

title: From Misuse to Mastery: Enhancing Code Generation with Knowledge-Driven AI Chaining
technique_name: KPC (Knowledge-driven Prompt Chaining)
core_idea_checked: Chain prompts that first extract API exception-handling knowledge from documentation, then condition code generation on it to handle exceptions correctly.
gain_metric: share of code meeting good exception-handling practice (manual CodeReview)
gain_quote: only 14.58% of code generated by ChatGPT can meet good exception handling practice, while that of our K PCbased approach is as high as 98.86%
gain_note: Exception handling maps only partly to R/M (closer to reliability). Manual review on 384 sampled tasks; LLMEva judge gives 34.30 vs 71.29.
benchmarks: 3,079 Java coding tasks derived from Java SDK & JDK API functional descriptions (384 sampled for manual review and EvoSuite); 92 Tutorialspoint tasks in the empirical study
models: GPT-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct)
note: Java API exception handling only; maps to robustness more than readability.

title: RAPGen: An Approach for Fixing Code Inefficiencies in Zero-Shot
technique_name: RAPGen (Retrieval-Augmented Prompt Generation)
core_idea_checked: Retrieve a fix-specific prompt template from a knowledge base mined from past performance fixes and use it to prompt the model zero-shot.
gain_note: Efficiency judged by match to developer fixes, not measured runtime; top-100 of 100 samples per task.
benchmarks: DeepDev-PERF C# performance-fix dataset, 132 instances; in-the-wild evaluation on 10 internal .NET services
models: gpt-3.5-turbo (closed, instruct)
note: C# performance fixes; Microsoft internal data partly.

title: Give LLMs a Security Course: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Knowledge Injection
technique_name: CodeGuarder (security knowledge base + query decomposition + CWE-prevalence re-ranking/filtering + prompt injection)
core_idea_checked: Builds a security knowledge base from vulnerability data, decomposes queries into sub-tasks, re-ranks and filters knowledge by CWE prevalence, and injects it into the generation prompt.
gain_metric: Security rate (CyberSecEval ICD), averaged across LLMs
gain_note: Average over six LLMs in the clean RACG setting; 20.12% is relative.
effect_correctness_headline: GPT-4o MBPP pass@1 from 72.8 to 73.2
benchmarks: CyberSecEval (1,916 instances, 50 CWEs; C, C++, Java, Python plus C#, JavaScript, PHP, Rust); MBPP; HumanEval
models: GPT-4o, closed, general; DeepSeek-V3 671B, open, general; CodeLlama-13B, open, code-specialized; DeepSeek-Coder-V2-16B, open, code-specialized; Mistral-7B, open; CodeLlama-7B, open, code-specialized

title: LLM Program Optimization via Retrieval Augmented Search
technique_name: Retrieval Augmented Search (RAS) with contextual retrieval
core_idea_checked: The LLM writes natural-language descriptions of programs to retrieve relevant slow-fast examples and uses them in an iterative search over candidate optimizations.
gain_quote: On PIE, RAS significantly outperforms dynamic retrieval, a state-of-the-art blackbox adaptation strategy, achieving an 8.70× average speedup compared to 4.23× for dynamic retrieval using Qwen3Coder.
gain_note: Edits human-written slow programs; LLM calls normalized across baselines; best-of-search speedup.
effect_correctness_headline: Mercury Pass@1 98.83 (RAS) vs 97.27 (No Contextual)
benchmarks: PIE C++ test set (973 programs); Mercury (256 test problems)
models: GPT-4o (closed); Qwen3-Coder 480B (open, code); DeepSeek V3.2 685B (open); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (open, instruct)
note: Code link is a project page; C++ on PIE. Same paper has AEGIS row (R01838#1).

title: SemOpt: LLM-Driven Code Optimization via Rule-Based Analysis
technique_name: SemOpt (strategy library + LLM-generated Semgrep rules + strategy-guided LLM optimization)
core_idea_checked: Builds a library of optimization strategies from historical commits, has the LLM write Semgrep rules to locate applicable code, and prompts the LLM to apply the matched strategy.
gain_metric: Semantic equivalence to developer optimization patch (SemEqv), C/C++, DeepSeek-V3
gain_note: Metric is match to developer optimization patches, not measured speedup; measured in-the-wild speedups (5.04%-218.07%) have no baseline. Edits human-written code.
effect_correctness_headline: 73.72% compile success and 72.43% test success on C/C++ projects; 100% test success on Python
benchmarks: Custom C/C++ benchmark of 151 tasks (40-task subset for Gemini); custom Python benchmark of 150 tasks; 5 C/C++ and 5 Python real-world projects
models: DeepSeek-V3-0324 (open, instruct); GPT-4.1 (closed); Gemini-2.5-Pro (closed, reasoning)
note: Repository-level optimization of C/C++ and Python projects.

title: AutoPatch: Multi-Agent Framework for Patching Real-World CVEs Generated by Outdated LLMs
technique_name: AutoPatch (Similarity Analyzer + Vulnerability Verifier + Code Patcher with CVE RAG DB and patch-verification loop)
core_idea_checked: Match generated code to known post-cutoff CVEs via a retrieval database, verify the vulnerability, then patch with the retrieved CVE fix context in a verify loop.
baseline_name: VSP (CoT with one-shot CWE example) on GPT-4o
gain_quote:
GPT-4o achieves
the highest patching accuracy at 94.12%, followed by o3mini at 87.07% and DeepSeek-R1 at 85.04%, showing the
strength of advanced language models in capturing and acting
upon vulnerability semantics. In contrast, VSP and the baseline
model exhibit significantly lower accuracies of 55.56% and
46.38%, respectively.
gain_note: Patch accuracy judgment method unclear (likely manual); functional correctness of patches not tested; only part of the dataset is LLM-generated.
benchmarks: Custom dataset: 525 snippets derived from 75 high-severity CVEs (late 2024-2025; 57 Linux kernel, 10 Chromium), including LLM re-implementations plus augmentations
models: GPT-4o (closed, instruct); o3-mini (closed, reasoning); DeepSeek-R1 32B (open, reasoning); code generation also by Code Llama 13b-instruct and DeepSeek Coder v2-lite

title: PEACE: Towards Efficient Project-Level Efficiency Optimization via Hybrid Code Editing
technique_name: PEACE (dependency-aware function sequence + valid associated edits agent + fine-tuned efficiency optimizer with internal/external retrieval)
core_idea_checked: Optimizes functions in dependency order, propagates valid associated edits across the project, and uses a fine-tuned optimizer with internal and external code retrieval.
gain_metric: opt rate (CPU instruction count relative to GPT-4o instruction prompting)
gain_quote: an impressive opt rate of +46.9%, surpassing all baselines by 18.4% to 39.1%.
gain_note: Opt rate is relative to a GPT-4o prompting baseline, not pre-optimization code; computed on correct cases only.
effect_correctness_headline: 69.2% pass@1 on PEACExec
benchmarks: PEACExec (new): 146 tasks from 47 Python GitHub projects (80 single-function, 66 multi-function)
models: Llama-3.1-405B (open, instruct); Llama3-8B LoRA fine-tuned optimizer (open); optimizer replaced in RQ4 by DeepSeek-V3-671B, GPT-4o, Claude-3.5, CodeLlama-13B fine-tuned
note: Project-level Python setting; uses a fine-tuned optimizer plus retrieval.

title: Enhancing Reliability in LLM-Based Secure Code Generation
technique_name: Mitigation-Aware Chain-of-Thought (MA-CoT)
core_idea_checked: Retrieves CWE mitigation guidance from a knowledge base and asks the model to reason through applicable mitigations in a chain of thought before coding.
gain_quote: MACoT reduces total security findings from 92 to 39 (57.6%) on the primary dataset
gain_note: Counts over three models, one sample each; generic security CoT baseline also reported; correctness not measured.
benchmarks: Primary dataset of 200 language-agnostic tasks (authors' prior dataset); LLMSecEval (150 tasks)
models: gpt-5-2025-08-07 (closed, reasoning); claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 (closed, instruct); gemini-2.5-pro (closed, reasoning)
note: Paper says code is on GitHub but gives no URL.

title: Planning with Large Language Models for Code Generation
technique_name: Planning-Guided Transformer Decoding (PG-TD) with code-length-penalty / comment-encouragement rewards
core_idea_checked: Use tree search during decoding with rewards that can penalize length or reward comments.
gain_quote: Default 248.42 0.68 23.14 by using different reward functions. Length Penalty 190.73
gain_note: Garbled table; side experiment.
effect_correctness_headline: APPS GPT-2 APPS Intro. pass rate 26.70 (PG-TD c=4) vs 11.95 beam search, 256 generations
benchmarks: APPS test (5000 problems: intro 1000, interview 3000, competition 1000); CodeContests test (165); HumanEval subset
models: APPS GPT-2 1.5B (fine-tuned, open); APPS GPT-Neo 2.7B (fine-tuned, open); Codex code-davinci-002 (closed, code)
note: Repo linked from paper's project page (codeaimcts.github.io); quality via length or comment rewards is a side experiment.

title: Constrained Decoding for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: Constrained Beam Sampling (positive/negative keyword and template constraints)
core_idea_checked: Beam sampling over code LLMs with manually specified positive and negative keyword/template constraints per prompt, enforcing secure API patterns during decoding.
baseline_name: SVEN prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (CodeGen-2.7B)
gain_quote: Our results show that constrained decoding over CodeGen (51.25% securepass@1) works better than prefix tuning with unconstrained decoding (36.3% secure-pass@1 for SVEN).
gain_note: Constraints written manually per prompt; same-model beam sampling baseline is 33.77, nucleus 26.07.
effect_correctness_headline: Llama3-8B pass@1 72.21 Constrained Beam vs 82.20 Beam
benchmarks: CodeGuard+ (91 prompts, 34 CWEs)
models: CodeGen-2.7B (open, code); SVEN (CodeGen-2.7B prefix-tuned); StarCoder2-3B; CodeGemma-7B; Llama3-8B; DeepseekCoder-33B; CodeLlama-34B; GPT-4 (closed, baseline only)
note: Constraints are hand-written per prompt, limiting transfer to new benchmarks.

title: Rethinking Repetition Problems of LLMs in Code Generation
technique_name: RPG (Repetition Penalization based on Grammar)
core_idea_checked: Detect repetition via grammar and penalize repeated statements during decoding.
gain_note: Vs greedy 0.631.
effect_correctness_headline: relative improvements of up to 11.3% in Pass@1 (HumanEval-ET, 0.258 vs Greedy 0.232)
benchmarks: CodeRepetEval (Artificial Synthesis 512, Code Generation Benchmarks 512, Real-world Repositories 1024; Go variant); HumanEval (164), HumanEval-ET, MBPP (974), MBPP-ET
models: CodeLlama-7B (open, code); CodeLlama-34B (open, code); CodeGen (open, code); DeepSeek-Coder (open, code); Llama2 (open, base)
note: Target is repetitive code (R/M); correctness also reported.

title: A Preliminary Study on the Robustness of Code Generation by Large Language Models
technique_name: RobGen (line-level intervention checker + token-level conditional logit adjustment of the 'if' token)
core_idea_checked: RobGen: a LoRA-SFT Qwen3-0.6B classifier trained on 12,000 GitHub Java blocks predicts whether the next line starts with 'if'; when positive and 'if' ranks within the top three, its logit is raised by delta*(rank-1) via a LogitsProcessor, with delta set to the 90th percentile of observed logit gaps per model.
gain_metric: Share of generated code judged less robust than the human reference by GPT-4o pairwise comparison (DeepSeekCoder-1.3B), %
gain_quote: for DeepSeekCoder-1.3B drops from 42.2% to 28.7%
gain_note: Section 4.1.2 text; per-method judge results for RobustCoder Prompt and Post-Generation Insertion appear only in Figure 9 without numbers. Table 3 average AvgABE (atomic boolean expressions, a gameable proxy): greedy 1.65, RobustCoder Prompt 1.73, PGI 2.06, RobGen 2.42 (w/o checker 3.41); average Pass@1 greedy 42.09, RobGen 43.57. Abstract headline: 'reduces the proportion of less robust code by 10%' across five models. CoderEval Java, 230 tasks, single greedy run; judge kappa 0.81 on 100 pairs.
effect_correctness_headline: achieves the highest average Pass@1 (43.57) vs 42.09 for greedy sampling
benchmarks: CoderEval Java, 230 repository-level tasks
models: DeepSeekCoder-1.3B-Instruct, open, code-specialized; DeepSeekCoder-6.7B-Instruct, open, code-specialized; Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct, open, code-specialized; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct, open, code-specialized; StarCoder2-7B, open, code-specialized
note: Half of the paper is an empirical robustness study, but RobGen is a reusable model-agnostic decoding plug-in with its own baselines and ablation; needs open-weight logits access.

title: A Mixture of Linear Corrections Generates Secure Code
technique_name: Mixture of Corrections (MoC): conditional, decayed activation steering vectors per CWE derived from linear probes (group mean diff, normal vector, PCA normal vector, dynamic NN)
core_idea_checked: Linear probes find vulnerability directions per CWE; a decaying mixture of correction vectors is added to hidden states only when the probe fires.
gain_metric: Security ratio SRh (CodeQL), SVEN test set
gain_quote: enhances the security ratio of Qwen2.5-Coder-7B by 8.9%, while simultaneously
gain_note: Best of four correction variants (Dynamic NN); 8.9 is percentage points; SVEN baseline weaker (65.0); single runs.
effect_correctness_headline: improving functionality on HumanEval pass@1 by 2.1% (QC-7B)
benchmarks: SVEN dataset (9 CWEs) test set for security; HumanEval for functionality
models: Qwen2.5-Coder-3B/7B/14B (open, code-specialized); Qwen2.5-Instruct-3B/7B/14B (open, instruct; transfer experiments)
note: Needs open-weight model hidden states; SVEN CWEs plus HumanEval.

title: Surprisal-Guided Selection: Compute-Optimal Test-Time Strategies for Execution-Grounded Code Generation
technique_name: Surprisal-guided Best-of-N selection (highest-surprisal correct sample; top3 variant)
core_idea_checked: Among correct samples, pick the one the model was least confident about (highest surprisal) instead of the most confident one.
gain_quote: This achieves 80% success (fast and correct) versus 50% for confidence-guided selection
gain_note: Only 10 task-seed pairs (p=0.125); fast_1 mixes correctness with speedup; single model; post-hoc analysis.
benchmarks: KernelBench L1 eval split; 2 subsets of 5 tasks for selection; full 20 tasks for Best-of-N
models: GPT-OSS-120B, open, with RLVR-trained LoRA (rank 16)
note: Evaluated only on 20 KernelBench L1 tasks; selection rule itself is domain-agnostic.

title: FunPRM: Function-as-Step Process Reward Model with Meta Reward Correction for Code Generation
technique_name: FunPRM (Chain-of-Function prompting + meta reward-corrected PRM Best-of-N selection)
core_idea_checked: Prompts the LLM to write code function by function, treating each function as a PRM step, and selects among N samples using a meta-learning-corrected PRM.
gain_metric: Human pairwise preference count (readability/reusability), correct solutions
gain_note: Figure-derived and garbled; labels suggest 54.2 FunPRM vs 45.8 base; marginal gain; no agreement statistic.
effect_correctness_headline: 80.9 pass@1 on LiveCodeBench (2025-02-01–present) with O4-mini (High)
benchmarks: LiveCodeBench v6 (454 problems after 2024-08-01; 131-problem subset after 2025-02-01); BigCodeBench (340-problem test split); HumanEval+; MBPP+
models: O4-mini (High), closed, reasoning; Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, open, code-specialized; GPT-4o-mini, closed, instruct; DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct, open, code-specialized; Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, open, code-specialized; PRM backbone Qwen2.5-Coder-7B with LoRA
note: Targets correctness; readability gain only from a small human preference study.

title: Interpreting and Steering for Safe and Correct Code Generation
technique_name: DuoSteer (double activation steering of safety and correctness directions at causally-identified attention heads)
core_idea_checked: Steer safety and correctness directions at causally identified attention heads.
gain_quote: In experiments over five vulnerability types, D UO STEER leads to an average of −26.9% vulnerability rate reduction and +7.5% functional correctness improvement, which outperforms not only other steering variants but also prompting and supervised fine-tuning baselin
gain_note: Relative (may be points); configs swept on eval set.
effect_correctness_headline: +7.5% functional correctness improvement (average); CWE-502 correctness = 94.1%
benchmarks: SecCodePLT held-out questions, 5 CWEs (022,079,094,295,502), 274 tasks; CodeSec-Pairs (9,342 pairs) for training directions

title: Security-by-Design for LLM-Based Code Generation: Leveraging Internal Representations for Concept-Driven Steering Mechanisms
technique_name: SCS-Code (Secure Concept Steering via difference-in-means residual stream activation addition)
core_idea_checked: Extracts a secure-code concept direction by difference in means of residual activations and adds it to the residual stream at inference to steer generation.
gain_note: Vs vanilla; hybrid with constrained decoding gives 27.9% relative gain on CWEval (Llama3.1-8B); correctness mixed.
effect_correctness_headline: Llama3 pass@1: 78.8(±0.5) with α=1 vs 75.9(±1.0) with α=0; CodeLlama pass@1: 65.7 vs 68.1

note: Needs open-weight model activations.

title: SecCodePRM: A Process Reward Model for Code Security
technique_name: SecCodePRM-guided inference-time scaling (step-level security PRM ranking candidates)
core_idea_checked: Train a process reward model that scores security at each code step, then use it to rank sampled candidates at inference time.
gain_note: Table fragment (Probability 41.64, QwenPRM 47.90, SecCodePRM 54.62); QC2.5-7B generator: 38.66 vs 42.86. SVEN results only in figure.
effect_correctness_headline: CWEval QC3-30B func@1: 78.15 vs Probability 67.06; LiveCodeBench QC2.5-32B pass@1 55.19% vs 53.23%

models: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (open, code-specialized) generator; Qwen2.5-Coder-32B; Qwen3-Coder-30B; SecCodePRM 7B verifier
note: Paper says code is available at a "SecCodePRM" hyperlink; URL lost in extraction.

title: Large Language Models for Code: Security Hardening and Adversarial Testing
technique_name: SVEN (security-hardening prefix-tuning with masked LM, contrastive and KL losses)
core_idea_checked: Learns small property-specific continuous prefixes via masked-LM, contrastive and KL losses on security-fix diffs, steering generation toward secure code without changing LM weights.
gain_metric: Security rate (% secure among valid programs, CodeQL)
gain_quote: SVENsec increases the security rate from 59.1% to 92.3%.
gain_note: Best-performing model size (2.7B), temperature 0.4; text-prompt and text-ft baselines are reported in ablations.
effect_correctness_headline: CodeGen-2.7B pass@1 14.0 (LM) vs 11.7 (SVENsec); pass@10 26.0 vs 24.7
benchmarks: Scenarios adapted from Pearce et al. (Asleep at the Keyboard) for 9 main CWEs (18 test scenarios); 4 unseen CWEs (12 scenarios) from Pearce et al.; 13 unseen CWEs (17 scenarios) from SecurityEval; CWE-089 prompt perturbations (16); HumanEval (164)
models: CodeGen-multi 350M, 2.7B, 6.1B (open, code-specialized base); InCoder 6.7B (open, code base); SantaCoder 1.3B (open, code base)

title: Instruction Tuning for Secure Code Generation
technique_name: SafeCoder (joint standard + security instruction tuning with masked NLL and unlikelihood loss)
core_idea_checked: Jointly instruction-tune on normal data and vulnerability-fix pairs, raising likelihood of secure tokens and applying unlikelihood loss to vulnerable tokens.
baseline_name: StarCoder-1B with standard instruction tuning (w/o SafeCoder)
gain_quote: StarCoder-1B n/a w/o SafeCoder with SafeCoder 55.6 62.9 92.1
gain_note: One of six models shown; gains do not generalize to unseen CWEs.

title: CodeUltraFeedback: An LLM-as-a-Judge Dataset for Aligning Large Language Models to Coding Preferences
technique_name: SFT + DPO (RLAIF) preference tuning on CodeUltraFeedback
core_idea_checked: Build a preference dataset where an LLM judge rates several LLMs' responses on five coding preferences, then align a code LLM with SFT and DPO on it.
gain_metric: LLM-judge score (1-10) for code complexity and efficiency preference, GPT-3.5-Turbo judge
gain_quote:
7.89 score on code complexity and efficiency preference, substantially surpassing CodeLlama-7B-Instruct
(6.16)

title: CodeDPO: Aligning Code Models with Self Generated and Verified Source Code
technique_name: CodeDPO (self-generated, self-validated preference data with PageRank-style code/test scoring plus execution-time pairs, trained with DPO/RPO)
core_idea_checked: Score self-generated code and tests with a PageRank-style mutual verification and add faster-vs-slower pairs, then train with DPO.

title: MPCoder: Multi-user Personalized Code Generator with Explicit and Implicit Style Representation Learning
technique_name: MPCoder (explicit coding-style residual learning + implicit style features + multi-user style adapter with contrastive learning)
core_idea_checked: Learn explicit (Checkstyle residual) and implicit style features per user and a contrastive multi-user adapter so generated code matches each user's coding style.
gain_note: Strongest baseline L-LDB nearly ties; vs CodeLlama 48.73. CSS is similarity to the user's own style.
